subject: FinLedger performance follow-up — concurrency & quota options
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@finledger.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jan 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FinLedger performance follow-up — concurrency & quota options

Hi Elena — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a recommended configuration and propose quota options: 

1) Recap of stated targets from your team:
- P99 latency target: <= 350ms for streaming LLM responses
- Sustained throughput: ~25 requests/sec (api-level requests)
- Peak concurrency: ~2,000 concurrent open sessions during market open spikes
- Streaming token throughput: ~800 tokens/sec aggregate

2) Clarifying questions (can you confirm):
- Are the 2,000 concurrent sessions long-lived (websocket/stream) or short-lived HTTP streaming?
- Do you plan to use persistent connection pooling with keep-alive on client side? If yes, what’s the average idle TTL you expect?
- Is there an expected read/write split or bursty synchronous patterns (e.g., many small requests vs fewer large streaming responses)?

3) Redwood options to consider (high level):
- Hosted API with negotiated rate limit increases and per-customer burst policy (fastest path to production; subject to quota approval)
- Dedicated Reserved capacity (predictable throughput and ability to set high concurrency caps; recommended for sustained high concurrency with SLOs)

Next steps: if you can answer the clarifying questions and attach a representative load profile (sample request sizes + open-session duration), Vivek and I will produce a capacity estimate and two options (hosted quota bump vs Dedicated sizing) with cost and expected SLOs.

I attached a blank load-profile CSV you can populate; feel free to drop the file or paste small samples into a reply.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: finledger-load-profile.csv
From: Elena Soto <elena@finledger.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@finledger.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jan 2025 11:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: FinLedger performance follow-up — concurrency & quota options

Hi Karthik — thanks for the recap. Answering inline below and attaching a short anonymized load export.

- Long-lived vs short-lived: These are mostly long-lived user sessions during trading hours. The sessions open when a user enters a workflow and remain open for 10–18 minutes on average; we do occasionally open secondary streams for real-time assistance.
- Connection pooling: Yes, we use a connection pool on our edge with keep-alives. Typical idle TTL is ~30s; we rotate connections per region.
- Request patterns: Mixture — 60% short prompt completions (3–30 tokens generated), 40% longer streaming responses (100–600 tokens). During spikes we see many short prompts in parallel (rapid-fire UI interactions).

Quantified numbers:
- Avg open sessions during market hours: 600–900 typical, peak historical 2,000 (we plan headroom to 2,500 for events)
- Avg requests/sec sustained: 25–40, with peaks to 300+ during certain events
- Streaming: aggregate token rate ~800 tokens/sec, with highest single-request streaming at ~1,200 tokens over ~20s
- SLA ask: p99 latency <= 350ms; p50 target 120ms

Regarding rate limits/quota negotiation: procurement (Tom) wants to understand whether Redwood will grant per-tenant burst allowances on the hosted plan or whether Dedicated is the only way to guarantee the concurrency/throughput required. If hosted with quota bump is feasible, what's the approval lead time and required commit (if any)? If Dedicated, we need a ballpark for committed throughput and monthly cost to socialize.

Attached: anonymized_load_export.csv

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Platform Engineering | FinLedger
elena@finledger.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@finledger.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jan 2025 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinLedger performance follow-up — concurrency & quota options

Hi Elena — appreciate the detailed numbers and the export. I ran a quick pass and sketched two practical options; attaching a short capacity estimate PDF. High level: 

Option A — Hosted (quota bump + burst policy):
- Feasibility: Possible for many patterns. We can provision a per-tenant burst allowance and increase rate limits to handle short spikes (requests/sec) up to ~300–500 for sustained short windows.
- Constraints: P99 streaming latency at <=350ms can be met for small-medium responses when there is idle capacity; during multi-hour market events with sustained high concurrency we risk SLO degradation if cluster-wide load is high.
- Lead time: 3–7 business days for quota approval and safety testing; requires a usage pass and signed mutual action plan.
- Pricing/commit: Typically no long-term commit required for moderate quota increases; larger reserved burst windows may need minimum monthly committed usage.

Option B — Dedicated Reserved capacity (recommended for sustained peaks):
- Feasibility: Strongest guarantee for concurrent long-lived streams and consistent p99 targets.
- Sizing note: Based on your load, a baseline 4-GPU pool (current generation xlarge) with autoscale headroom looks appropriate to cover sustained 25–40 RPS and peaks to 300 RPS with concurrency headroom to 2,500 sessions.
- Lead time: 2–3 weeks to provision (region, networking, and customer onboarding).
- Commit: Monthly reserved contract; we’ll provide a pricing worksheet.

Open items I need from you to finalize sizing:
- Sample distribution of tokens per request (we have the export, but need per-request percentile if possible)
- Confirmation on whether all sessions originate from a single region or multiple regions (affects replication and capacity split)
- Any regulatory constraints for logging retention that would increase CPU/memory on the host side

I attached capacity-estimate-20250119.pdf and our rate-limit explainer. Happy to hop on a sizing call Tue/Wed next week. If procurement prefers to start with a hosted quota bump to buy time, we can draft a temporary MAPlan that includes a clear migration path to Dedicated.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Attachments: capacity-estimate-20250119.pdf, redwood-rate-limit-explainer.pdf
From: Elena Soto <elena@finledger.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@finledger.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jan 2025 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinLedger performance follow-up — concurrency & quota options

Thanks Vivek — this is very helpful. We reviewed internally and procurement would like to see two things before a decision: 1) a short hosted-path MAPlan with explicit burst windows and escalation terms, and 2) a Dedicated pricing estimate (monthly commit + expected overage model).

We agree Dedicated is the safer route for predictable SLOs; procurement and engineering will evaluate the hosted temporary path if the MAPlan provides clear SLAs during the transition. Please include Tom (procurement) on the pricing/contract thread — Tom, looping you in to start collecting contract requirements.

We can do a quick sizing call Tuesday 2025-01-21 at 10:00am PT if that works for your team. We'll bring the quant dev who owns the connection pool.

I'll upload a per-request percentile export to the shared folder before the call.

Best,
Elena Soto
Director of Platform Engineering | FinLedger
elena@finledger.com
